source.title: Hidden Synergy: L1 Weight Normalization and 1-Path-Norm Regularization

record.tranche_reason: Reports training and test performance for overparameterized networks under different capacity-control methods, but does not test the specific versioned claims.
record.gate_note: The Fashion-MNIST ablation reports train and test cross-entropy for seven models. Tabular test-set results and cited prior-work findings do not provide a direct test of the listed versions. The paper mentions batch size effects on near-sparsity, not on the generalization gap.
record.test_reason: The study tests its proposed normalization, capacity-control and pruning methods, but none of V1–V8. Natural-label train/test performance alone does not test V1; path-norm regularization does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. Batch-size experiments report near-sparsity, not held-out performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that weight normalization makes 1-path-norm regularization practical in overparameterized networks, that their improved CReLU residual bound improves generalization in the tested ablation, and that PSiLON models are competitive on small tabular datasets. They additionally conclude that L1 normalization and path-norm regularization promote near-sparsity and that late pruning achieves exact sparsity while retaining performance.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces L1 weight normalization, length parameter sharing, and 1-path-norm regularization; experiments use tabular data and Fashion-MNIST rather than the settings in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: On Fashion-MNIST, improved-bound models perform better than original-bound and standard models; the paper attributes the Pj-ResNet result partly to optimization difficulty and notes slower convergence for L1 than L2 normalization under a fixed compute budget.

fits_no_version.finding: On Fashion-MNIST, improved-bound models achieve test cross-entropies of 0.403–0.419, compared with 0.439–0.477 for original-bound models and 0.492 for S-ResNet, under a fixed 20,000-update budget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization and normalization choices affect held-out performance in the tested overparameterized, fully connected CReLU residual networks.

fits_no_version.finding: On Higgs, P-Net achieves test cross-entropy 0.616 versus S-Net's 0.693; finer tuning improves the L2-regularized comparators to 0.646. A final pruning stage yields 0.614 and exact sparsity 0.817.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this small-data tabular setting, the proposed capacity-control recipe improves held-out loss over the tested L2 recipes, and late weight pruning retains its performance.

record.problems: The experiments use small-data tabular datasets and a single Fashion-MNIST ablation, with a fixed compute budget and validation-selected regularization. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper does not test random-label fitting or the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example claims.
record.rows_left_out: Other tabular test-set values in Tables 1 and 2 are not extracted because they report test performance without paired training metrics or a direct generalization-gap comparison; cited findings are excluded.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or comparison of random-label and natural-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe.
No width sweep beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of learned local connectivity.
Adam is used throughout; no adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison.
Batch size is varied at fixed update count, with near-sparsity reported; no held-out performance comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, gap-ranking analysis or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No identification and removal of memorized training examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version, but supplies no direct test of them. Its generalization claims concern a different regularization method; they do not justify version-level verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label comparison.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison; the conclusion says convolutional layers are not addressed.
Adam is used, but no optimizer comparison is reported.
No large-batch generalization-gap comparison; batch size is varied only for near-sparsity.
No removal of memorized training examples.
